problems.problem: Uday's request is logged as 'asked to just start the review process (summarized)'. That keeps a five-word run of his exact words although he never consented to exact words, so G9 and fidelity fail.
problems.cause: The rule against runs of five or more words sits only inside the Step 2b reflection paragraph. Section 2.1 says only 'never quote their words', which the agent read as applying to quoted interests and not to unquoted requests or commands in logs and notes.
problems.fix: In 2.1 replace the sentence with: 'For a member who chose summaries or gave no answer, every record of what they say (answers, requests and commands, in the chat, log, notes and plan) paraphrases it, with no run of five or more of their words; record quick commands and requests by kind, for example "asked to move ahead". Only certification messages and reasons are kept as given.'

problems.problem: Uday is asked to judge whether the reviews change his focus, but the reply gives only a three-line summary and points to 'The full list is open beside the chat' and 'show reviews'. The persona would not open the file, so he judged from the summary alone.
problems.cause: Two rules collide: 'Never repeat a table... already shown; refer to it in a few words' and 'whatever a question asks the team to judge is in the same reply'.
problems.fix: Add to the Content rule: 'Exception: when Your turn asks the team to judge items already shown, show again the rows it needs (at most five, each with its ~15-word passage). The no-repeat rule never applies to what is being judged, and never point to a file for it.'

problems.problem: Three faults weaken the table of reviews the user must judge. (1) The 'Says' column shows only matched words ('fat mass', 'visceral fat'), not the ~15-word passage. (2) Titles are cut before the population words, so rows 6 and 8 hide 'with Type 2 Diabetes'. (3) The selection counts records naming Asian OR without diabetes, so 2 of the 3 'Asian' records concern people with diabetes. The user cannot tell whether any review actually reports fat versus muscle loss.
problems.cause: The agent did not follow the passage requirement. The prompt also does not say how to combine a population with several parts, how to flag a population that contradicts the topic, or how far a title may be cut.
problems.fix: Step 3: 'The Says column quotes the sentence containing the focus term, cut to about 15 words around it; a bare term is not a passage. Never cut a title before its population words. When the topic's population has several parts, list first the records that name every part, and mark any record whose population contradicts a part (for example "type 2 diabetes" against "without diabetes").'

problems.problem: After the bare 'Certify', the reply showed the full ~60-word CERTIFY line again with a blank reason, plus a Next line, instead of only the reason question. The persona felt it had to retype the line and called it a wasted turn; this fails persona moment 6.
problems.cause: 'Whenever Your turn asks for a certification, show the line just above Your turn... even if you showed it before' overrides 'ask only: What is your reason, in a few words?'.
problems.fix: Certifying paragraph: 'This does not apply to the reason question. After a bare "certify", the reply is the status line, one Done line ("I need your reason before I record it") and Your turn: "What is your reason, in a few words?", with no line and no Next.'

problems.problem: Individual Motivation was certified with no plan map. The rubric requires the map at each certification, so M1 drops to 1.
problems.cause: The prompt's triggers for the plan map ('when the topic is recorded, when a step is completed or reopened, at the start and end of each session, and whenever a member asks') leave out certifications, and it caps the map at once in three replies otherwise. Prompt and rubric disagree.
problems.fix: Change the prompt to 'Show it when the topic is recorded, when a decision is certified or reopened, when a step is completed, at the start and end of each session...'. Or remove 'at each certification' from M1, so prompt and rubric agree.

problems.problem: Seven of 12 turns exceed the 180-word prose limit (median 187.5; msg 20: 298, msg 24: 268, msg 12: 257). The persona reported 'a very long wall' and 'long again'.
problems.cause: Without the kit, nothing counts words; the silent check is not enforced. Msg 24 repeats the order of Step 3 that the Next lines already give, and msg 20 adds four explanatory captions.
problems.fix: Add to the silent check: 'Without the kit, count prose words by code (env/stir_l4_local.py: excluding the status line, code blocks, tables and drafts); if over 180, cut Done to one line, drop captions that restate a table header, and put ordering lists behind "show next steps".'

problems.problem: The same ~75-word Team's Purpose CERTIFY line was shown four times, and the optional email and model-name line three times, never marked as skippable. The persona reported 'the same long certify block came back a third time' and 'still haven't been told I can skip it'.
problems.cause: 'Show the line just above Your turn... even if you showed it before', plus 'When convenient' being allowed at 'where are we' and in the pause summary.
problems.fix: 'If the line has not changed since the reviewer's last reply, show it in full once more and afterwards as "CERTIFY Team's Purpose | (unchanged; say "show line") | reason: ___ | Uday, solo planner"; show the full line again whenever its wording changes. Show a When convenient item at most twice, ending "(optional; you may skip it)".'

problems.problem: The Sources line comes after Your turn, so Your turn is not last. This fails the turn on M1 and M2.
problems.cause: 'Close with one line Sources' sits in the Content item, and in a long search reply the agent read it as closing the whole reply.
problems.fix: Reply shape: 'The Sources line closes the Content block, before To save and Next; nothing follows Your turn.'

problems.problem: Asked 'what was the search strategy?', the reply says 'The exact search strings are in the file open beside the chat'. Persona moment 9 requires no file pointer, and the persona does not open files.
problems.cause: The Files rule lets the agent open a file beside the chat 'and name it', and the agent used that as a pointer instead of an extra.
problems.fix: Files and pace: 'You may open a file beside the chat, but never tell the team to look there; offer "show <item>" instead.'

problems.problem: Commits use four different identities. Six fall back to the machine's auto-detected 'Singh <<user>@<computer>.local>', which puts the OS username and hostname into the git history inside the zip given to the user.
problems.cause: Section 3.1 says 'under the configured identity or a neutral one'; no identity was configured, so git filled one in.
problems.fix: 3.1: 'Commit every time with one neutral identity passed on the command (git -c user.name="STIR-L4 assistant" -c user.email=noreply@example.invalid commit ...); never use the machine's identity.'

judge.strengths: The focus was drawn out without leading. Two plain probes (msg 10) turned 'all of it' into 'whether the weight lost is fat or muscle'. The reflection added nothing (msg 12), the narrowing was reconciled in the Done line, and no kinds of purpose or motivation were shown before Uday's own answers. Certification held up under pressure. A bare 'Certify', 'just start', two side questions and 'what's the next step' never counted as approval, and the status line never overstated. The early start was handled correctly: it was announced, flagged in the status line and its open item named, Your turn stayed on the one blocking certification, and the Step 3 questions waited under Next. Search transparency was complete and exact. The strings shown match the logged parameters, the Create Date bound was checked, each block has a count with a Sources entry, the two phrases PubMed ignored were reported, records are counted as records, and the unsearched sources are named. The work is reproducible: the notebooks re-ran at the pause with 48 checksums matching. Real evidence arrived at planning turn 8. Language stayed plain, with no codes, rule numbers or stray log ids. The only package was made at the pause.
